16161: The RB1 heading into 2026 after a historic 2025 — 2,298 scrimmage yards, 11 TDs, and a league-leading 366 touches across 17 games. The only player in NFL history with 1,400 rushing yards and 800+ receiving yards in the same season. Contracted at $63 in year 4 of 5 — about $2 below fair market for what is arguably the best back in football.
16211: The WR1 in fantasy in 2025 — 129 catches, 1,715 yards, 10 TDs on 166 targets across 16 games, the highest receiving yards-per-game average in NFL history. Reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford just signed a one-year, $55M extension to stay in LA through 2027, cementing the most important relationship for Nacua's fantasy value. Contracted at $19 in year 4 of 5, over $31 below fair market — one of the better value contracts in the league.
16185: Put together one of the great WR seasons in recent memory in 2025 — 119 catches, 1,793 receiving yards (NFL-high), 10 TDs, and a Super Bowl ring in Seattle. WR2 in total fantasy scoring, averaging 21.2 PPG. contracted at $34 in year 4 of 6, a meaningful discount for the focal point of the Seahawks' passing attack.
16162: Posted 1,839 scrimmage yards and 18 TDs in 2025 — the most touchdowns of any running back in the NFL. His 22.7 PPR points per game was a career high and ranked second overall at any position. Contracted at $55 in year 4 of 5, roughly fair value for a player with legitimate RB1 ceiling every week.
15287: Finished WR4 in 2025 fantasy scoring and is firmly in the elite tier heading into 2026. A model of consistency in Detroit's high-powered offense, St. Brown enters the final year of a six-year deal at $33. good value on the books — he's $13 below market — but the expiring contract makes this a pivotal season.
13130: Still the gold standard at running back despite turning 30 in 2026. Entering year 2 of 3 at $63, he's $6 above fair market — a modest overpay for a player whose floor remains elite even as questions about his age and touch count grow. The bet on sustaining the window; how that plays out depends on CMC's health.
14832: Posted another dominant season in Dallas with Prescott healthy and Pickens pulling attention away. Firmly in the WR4-6 conversation heading into 2026. contracted at $48 in year 2 of 3, only $4 above curve — essentially fair value for one of the most complete receivers in the game.
14836: A down 2025 after years of elite production — 84 catches for 1,048 yards and just 2 TDs as J.J. McCarthy worked through his development as a starter in Minnesota. The talent and route running are unchanged, but the production took a significant step back. WR5 heading into 2026 on the strength of his track record and upside. On the books at $68 in year 2 of 3 — $25 above fair market, a real overpay if the 2025 numbers are the new baseline rather than a blip.
14802: RB4 coming off a big 2025 season that justified his $56 auction price. Now at $59 in year 2 of 3, just $7 above the market curve — essentially fair value for a top-5 back. Both sides are reportedly having productive conversations about his future. The anchor of that backfield and one of the more interesting contract situations in the league.
15290: The WR8 in PPR heading into 2026 after another elite season in Houston's high-volume offense. Nico Collins has become one of the more reliable weekly starters in the league. Contracted at $32 in the final year of a 6-year deal — $8 below fair market, excellent value heading into a contract year.
16615: The Giants' WR1 and a legitimate breakout threat in year 3 of 5. Ranked WR9 heading into 2026 after steadily improving production in New York. On the books at $21 — over $16 below what the curve says he should cost. One of the best value contracts in the league at this ECR.
16167: Career year in 2025 — 1,838 scrimmage yards, 12 TDs, PFF's RB1 overall. Now in year 4 of 5 at $23, a staggering $22.60 below his market curve. One of the best value contracts in the league and arguably in the league. Some uncertainty around Miami's QB situation heading into 2026 but Achane's volume should keep him elite regardless.
16194: The talent has never been in question — 79 catches for 938 yards and 7 TDs as a rookie, followed by a knee injury in 2024 and a 6-game suspension to open 2025. When he returned last year he posted 53 catches, 571 yards, and 5 TDs in 11 games, showing flashes of what he can be. The off-field situation is the real story: 30 days in jail starting May 19 for a probation violation (THC positive), a pending civil lawsuit filed by a former girlfriend, and a right knee cleanup surgery expected to sideline him two months. He's expected to be available for training camp but enters 2026 in the final year of his rookie contract with genuine uncertainty about his future in Kansas City. High ceiling, very high risk.
15762: Landed in Dallas alongside Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb and immediately produced as a legitimate WR1. WR11 heading into 2026 at just 24 years old. contracted at $24 in year 2 of 3 — about $11 below what the market would pay. The best contract on their roster with one year until free agency.
17042: The Las Vegas Raiders' star RB and a legitimate RB6 in fantasy heading into 2026. Jeanty had a dominant rookie season and is contracted at $38 in year 2 of 5 — $4 below curve. Multi-year cost control on a player already ascending toward the top tier.
15715: Led the NFL in rushing yards in 2025 — 309 carries, 1,621 yards, 12 TDs — and won the league rushing title. One of the best backs in football and the engine of Buffalo's offense. In year 2 of a 4-year extension signed before the 2025 season. Contracted at $38 in year 2 of 4, fair value for a rushing champion.
15754: The WR14 in fantasy heading into 2026 after a quietly excellent season in New Orleans. Chris Olave is in year 2 of 3 at just $11 — over $21 below his market curve. One of the most underpaid contracts in the entire league. Whoever retains him is in a strong position.
16641: The TE2 overall heading into 2026, Brock Bowers put together one of the great tight end seasons in recent memory as a rookie. Now in year 3 of 6 at $9 — over $21 below curve. An absolute steal at this price — arguably the best tight end value in the league on a long-term deal.
16181: Chase Brown emerged as Cincinnati's featured back and has climbed to RB8 in fantasy heading into 2026. Consistent volume and solid efficiency make him a reliable starter. on the books at $21 in year 4 of 6 — nearly $17 below curve, excellent long-term value.
14104: Traded to New England on June 1 after a lengthy saga that was the worst-kept secret in the NFL. The Patriots sent picks to Philadelphia to land their new WR1, reuniting Brown with head coach Mike Vrabel — who drafted him in Tennessee in 2019. Brown turns 29 this month and brings six 1,000-yard seasons, three Pro Bowls, and a Super Bowl ring to Foxborough. He steps into an offense with Drake Maye at quarterback and Romeo Doubs as a complementary piece — a significant upgrade in situation. The question is whether his numbers hold up away from a premium Philly offense. On the books at $42 in year 2 of 3, above fair market for a WR who may be trending toward his mid-career plateau.
13589: The QB1 in fantasy for the second straight year, Josh Allen remains the most valuable quarterback in the game — elite rushing upside, big arm, command of one of the best offenses in the NFL. Acquired via trade last offseason, currently at $24 in year 2 of 3 — a bargain at $6 below curve for the top player at his position.
17044: The Chargers' RB1 emerging as one of the more exciting backs in football heading into year 2. Omarion Hampton is already RB9 in early 2026 rankings and in a high-usage role in LA. contracted at $28 in year 2 of 5 — $7 below curve — with four more years of control ahead.
17071: Finished his rookie season as WR14 — ahead of schedule by most measures. One year into a five-year deal at $18, McMillan is Carolina's unquestioned WR1 at 6'4" with exceptional catch radius. on the books at $10 below his market curve. The cornerstone piece of the roster going forward.
13604: Won Super Bowl LIX with Philadelphia in his first Eagles season — posting 2,005 rushing yards and 13 TDs in the regular season, breaking the NFL record for most rushing yards in a single season including postseason. Named Offensive Player of the Year. Still putting up elite numbers as the RB10 heading into 2026. On the books at $68 in year 2 of 3 — $35 above fair market, the largest absolute overpay on any roster. Barkley is worth it on the field; the contract situation will be worth watching.
13593: A disappointing 2025 — limited to 13 games by back and hamstring injuries, finishing with just 2,549 passing yards, 21 TDs, and a career-low 349 rushing yards. On the books at $37 in the final year of a 3-year deal, $10 above fair market. A clear bounce-back candidate if healthy, but the Ravens finished 8-9 and missed the playoffs entirely in 2025.
15753: Now in the Jets' improved passing attack, Garrett Wilson continues to be one of the most technically gifted receivers in the league. WR15 heading into 2026. contracted at $17 in year 2 of 3 — nearly $9 below curve, excellent value for a player with clear upside.
15282: DeVonta Smith remains one of the sharpest route runners in the NFL, providing reliable production in Philadelphia's still-potent offense. WR16 heading into 2026. contracted at $16 in year 2 of 3 — $9 below curve.
16580: The QB3 heading into 2026 after a breakout second season in New England. Drake Maye has the arm talent and mobility to challenge Josh Allen at the top of the position long-term. contracted at $6 in year 3 of 6 — nearly $18 below curve. The best young QB contract in the league.
16627: Los Angeles Chargers WR who quietly put together one of the more efficient seasons at the position. Ladd McConkey is WR18 heading into 2026 in a pass-heavy offense. contracted at $14 in year 3 of 5 — $8 below curve, solid value.
14073: RB13 heading into 2026 after two productive seasons in Green Bay — 2,882 scrimmage yards and 30 TDs combined. On the books at $54 in year 2 of 3 — $28 above fair market, the most significant overpay on the roster. Jacobs' attorneys deny the allegations and the investigation is ongoing, but an NFL suspension is a real possibility. The Packers have no guaranteed money remaining on his deal, leaving his roster status genuinely uncertain heading into the season.
17104: The TE3 heading into 2026 after a standout rookie season in Chicago. Colston Loveland is widely regarded as one of the best values at the position going forward. contracted at $6 in year 2 of 6 — $15 below curve, exceptional long-term value.
16190: The WR19 heading into 2026 in Baltimore's productive passing game. Zay Flowers provides consistent production and red-zone value in a balanced Ravens offense. contracted at $13 in year 4 of 6 — $7 below curve.
17070: A standout rookie in Chicago's offense, Luther Burden is already the WR20 heading into year 2. One of the best value contracts in the league at $3 in year 2 of 6 — $17 below curve. Multi-year cost control available on a rising star.
15284: Spent 2025 in Miami posting 64 catches for 910 yards and 6 TDs before being traded to Denver during the 2026 draft for the Broncos' first-round pick. Now 27 years old, he joins a Broncos team that went 14-3 in 2025 and lost in the AFC Championship. His contract runs through 2028 — a legitimate long-term piece for a Denver team built to contend.
12626: Derrick Henry is still a force at RB14 heading into 2026, defying every age-related expectation in Baltimore. But at $53 in year 2 of 3, he's $31 above his market curve — one of the largest absolute overpays in the league. Vintage prices on the books for a player heading into his age-32 season.
15708: Breece Hall remains one of the more dynamic backs in the league when healthy, ranking RB15 heading into 2026 in the Jets' improving offense. Contracted at $26 in year 2 of 3 — $4 above fair market, modest overpay for the production.
14777: The QB4 in fantasy, Joe Burrow remains one of the most dangerous quarterbacks in football when healthy. His injury history is the only concern. contracted at $14 in year 2 of 3 — $5 below curve, solid value if he stays on the field.
17081: Tampa Bay's emerging WR1, Emeka Egbuka is the WR24 heading into year 2 and a prime breakout candidate. contracted at $13 in year 2 of 5 — $4 below curve, with four more years of control ahead.
15253: Travis Etienne landed in New Orleans and has established himself as a reliable every-down back. RB16 heading into 2026. contracted at $13 in year 2 of 3 — $7 below curve, solid value.
15710: Kyren Williams is the Rams' primary back and a consistent fantasy starter, ranking RB17 heading into 2026. contracted at $20 in year 5 of 6 — essentially at fair value with one year left after this.
11671: A legendary career — 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons from 2014-2024 before injuries limited him to 8 games in 2025 (hamstring, broken collarbone). Now in his first season with San Francisco after signing a 3-year, $60M deal in free agency. At 32, the big question is whether he can return to full health after the most injury-plagued season of his career.
15756: Jameson Williams is WR26 heading into 2026 after a breakout season in Detroit. Big-play threat with elite speed. contracted at $29 in year 2 of 3 — $14 above curve, a real overpay unless the big plays keep coming.
16598: Bucky Irving emerged as Tampa Bay's featured back and is RB19 heading into year 3. contracted at $14 in the final year of a 3-year deal — $3 below curve, modest value in a contract year.
16581: Heading into his third NFL season carrying a significant injury question mark. A knee sprain, hamstring injury, and dislocated elbow limited Daniels to just seven games in 2025, and the Commanders shut him down entirely for the final three weeks of the season. When healthy in year one he was one of the most electrifying QBs in football. The talent is not in question — durability is. Still contracted at $14 in year 3 of 5, making him one of the most intriguing upside plays at the position if he can stay on the field.
17102: Tyler Warren is the Colts' young TE and already TE4 heading into year 2. contracted at $6 in year 2 of 5 — $9 below curve, significant value on a long-term contract for a player still ascending.
17472: The consensus 1.01 in the FBP rookie draft. Notre Dame RB who landed with Arizona — a backfield he should own immediately as the Cardinals' featured back. At 6'0", 212 lbs with vision, power, and pass-catching ability, Love profiles as a legitimate top-5 fantasy RB as a rookie. The best prospect in a thin RB class by a wide margin.
17497: The WR1 in the class, drafted 4th overall by Tennessee. Polished, pro-ready route runner from Ohio State with big hands and a large wingspan. Steps into a clear opportunity as Cam Ward's top target with the Titans. Year 2 of Ward's development should help. Projected around 70 catches for 924 yards and 5 TDs in year 1 — borderline WR2 with WR1 upside.
17498: Went 8th overall to New Orleans, pairing with Chris Olave and second-year QB Tyler Shough. At 6'2", 203 lbs, Tyson is a versatile, prototypical target who led the class with a 35% target share in 2025 at Arizona State. Often compared to George Pickens. Steps into an immediate role in an offense loaded with young talent — high ceiling if Shough takes the expected Year 2 leap.
17499: Slipped to Philadelphia at pick 20 despite being considered by many the most talented receiver in the class. A dominant slot technician — posted 3.04 yards-per-route-run at USC, the class-best mark. Steps in alongside DeVonta Smith with A.J. Brown likely departing. Volume is there, though the Eagles' run-heavy scheme is a mild concern. Elite PPR floor.
17473: Notre Dame teammate of Jeremiyah Love, drafted 32nd by Seattle to fill the void left by Kenneth Walker's departure. With Zach Charbonnet recovering from an ACL tear, Price steps into an immediate lead back role for a Seahawks team that wants to run. RB2 in the rookie class and a legitimate top-5 pick in the FBP rookie draft.
17501: Browns WR with explosive after-catch ability and elite athleticism — averaged 7.2 yards after catch per reception at Texas A&M in 2025. High-volume PPR weapon in Todd Monken's system, which he ran at Baltimore with Zay Flowers. The QB situation in Cleveland is the primary risk, but Concepcion has the upside to be a target magnet for years. One of the more dynamic receivers in the class.
17502: Jets WR drafted as a long-needed slot complement to Garrett Wilson. Good after-catch ability with legitimate WR2 ceiling over time. The Jets' receiver room is suddenly crowded — Wilson, Sadiq, and Cooper all competing for targets — which caps his immediate upside. One to monitor for Year 2.
17543: First-round TE prospect (Jets) with freakish athleticism — 4.39 speed, 43.5" vertical, 133" broad jump. Projects as a slot-aligned receiving tight end in New York's offense. 17462: The QB1 in the rookie class, drafted by Las Vegas. Raised eyebrows with a standout pre-draft process and should compete for the starting role early. A dual-threat prospect with strong arm talent — the kind of long-term dynasty piece this league rewards. Year 1 production depends on how fast he wins the job.
17544: Second-round TE to Philadelphia, arriving as a potential heir to Dallas Goedert. One of the more intriguing sleeper TEs in the class.
17500: Browns WR who pairs with KC Concepcion to give Cleveland a potentially dangerous young receiver duo. At 6'4", 209 lbs, Boston brings rare size and posted back-to-back 800+ yard seasons at Washington in 2024-25. Could line up as the outside receiver and earn immediate targets. Underrated dynasty pick at this range.
17477: RB3 in the rookie class, drafted by Denver. Part of the third tier of rookie backs but lands in a situation worth monitoring depending on the Broncos' depth chart. More of a year 2-3 dynasty investment than an immediate starter.
17512: Commanders WR with solid size and athleticism. Lands in Washington's pass-heavy offense as a day 2 selection. WR7 in the rookie class with solid mid-round dynasty value. One to watch if targets open up.
17463: The QB2 in the rookie class, drafted by the Rams. Talented dual-threat passer who lands behind Matthew Stafford — likely a year or two away from starting. Long-term dynasty upside worth investing in for a keeper league.
17474: RB5 in the class, drafted by Kansas City. Joins the Chiefs' backfield in a committee situation. Kenneth Walker's arrival could limit his immediate ceiling, but his receiving ability fits Andy Reid's scheme well. Depth value with upside.
15281: The overall WR1 heading into 2026 — and one of the most significant players available at auction this offseason. Posted 125 catches, 1,412 yards, and 8 TDs on a league-leading 185 targets in 2025, even with Burrow missing time due to injury. With Burrow healthy, Chase becomes an argument for the best player in fantasy football. Third player ever with 125+ catches in back-to-back seasons. Expect a heated auction if he becomes available.
15751: Atlanta's WR1 and one of the most target-heavy receivers in the league — 112 targets across just 12 games in 2025, averaging 9.3 targets per game over the last two seasons. Knee injury cut his year short but he still managed 68-919-7. At 24 years old he's entering his prime. The ongoing QB uncertainty in Atlanta (Tua Tagovailoa) is the main knock, but the volume has always been there regardless.
15794: Set an NFL record for most catches by a tight end in a single season in 2025 — 126 receptions, 1,239 yards, 11 TDs. The undisputed TE1 heading into 2026 in both PPR and dynasty formats. Commands a 25%+ target share in Arizona and just signed the richest TE contract in NFL history. If available at auction, he won't come cheap — and he shouldn't. Jeremiyah Love lands in Arizona and could draw some targets away at the goal line, but McBride's role is secure.
14783: Five-year NFL veteran who remains one of the most complete quarterbacks in the game — elite rushing floor with consistent passing volume. Threw for 3,224 yards and 25 TDs in 2025 with 8 rushing scores, finishing as a QB1 despite an inconsistent Eagles offense. At QB6 heading into 2026, he's a reliable starter with a high floor. On the books at $28 in year 2 of 3.
14779: One of the most talented pure passers in the league, Herbert has been tantalizingly consistent without ever quite breaking through to the elite tier. Finished as a QB7 in 2025 in a Chargers offense that should improve under new OC Mike McDaniels. Contracted at $36 in year 2 of 3 — significantly above fair market for his current ranking, but the talent ceiling keeps him relevant.
17032: Breakout second-year QB for the Giants who finished as a legitimate QB1 option down the stretch of 2025. His dual-threat ability gives him a rushing floor that keeps his weekly ceiling high — averaging 18.9 PPR points per game even when removing designed carries. Now the QB8 heading into 2026. Contracted at $10 in year 2 of 5 — one of the best value QB contracts in the league.
16579: Took a significant step forward in his second NFL season under Ben Johnson, finishing as QB7 in points per game in 2025. Closed the year playing his best football. At 24 years old with a top offensive mind coaching him, the trajectory points toward a legitimate top-5 QB in coming seasons. Contracted at $16 in year 3 of 5, a fair value for a rapidly ascending talent.
15237: Finally put it all together in his first season under Liam Coen, posting career highs in passing TDs (29) and rushing scores (9) to finish as QB4 in scoring over the final seven weeks of 2025. The talent was always there; the coaching and system matters enormously here. QB10 overall heading into 2026 and could outperform that ranking with another year of development. Contracted at $22 in year 4 of 5.
12620: Model of consistency — led the NFL in completions in 2025, set career highs in passing yards and attempts, and finished with his highest rate of 21+ point games since 2019. At QB11 heading into 2026, Prescott benefits from one of the best receiver combinations in the league in Lamb and Pickens. Contracted at $42 in year 2 of 3, a significant overpay relative to his current ranking.
15698: Has posted QB8, QB12, and QB6 finishes in points per game over the last three seasons — one of the more quietly reliable QB1 options in the league. Elite efficiency in a Kyle Shanahan system, with added rushing value. QB12 heading into 2026. Contracted at $18 in year 2 of 3, near fair market for the production.
15711: Super Bowl MVP who signed with Kansas City after his time in Seattle. Steps into a promising situation with the Chiefs, who have historically deployed a featured back in their offense. RB11 heading into 2026, Walker's receiving ability makes him a strong fit in Andy Reid's scheme. Contracted at $26 in year 2 of 3.
15256: One of the more dynamic backs in football when healthy, Williams carved out a significant role in Dallas and finished as RB18 heading into 2026. His receiving ability out of the backfield keeps his PPR ceiling high in an offense with Dak Prescott, Lamb, and Pickens. Contracted at $14 in year 4 of 5.
17045: Impressive rookie season for the Giants in 2025, establishing himself as one of the more exciting young backs in football. Now RB20 heading into year 2 with New York committed to featuring him in their offense. A leg fracture late in 2025 is the primary concern — recovery and health will determine his 2026 ceiling. Contracted at $6 in year 2 of 5.
17043: Stepped into an immediate role with New England and showed RB1 flashes in his rookie season, finishing as RB21 heading into 2026. His receiving ability is elite — one of the best pass-catching backs in the class. Contracted at $6 in year 2 of 5, potentially one of the most undervalued contracts in the league if he takes the expected Year 2 leap.
14071: Moved to Houston and stepped into a full-time role, finishing as RB22 heading into 2026. Montgomery has been a durable, efficient back throughout his career — a reliable 15-carry floor who doesn't lose games. Contracted at $14 in year 2 of 3. Affordable for the production he delivers.
14797: Landed in Chicago and has established himself as a reliable RB in a decent Bears offense. Finished as RB23 heading into 2026 — a consistent low-end RB1 who doesn't excite but doesn't disappoint. Contracted at $9 in year 3 of 3, final year of the deal.
17051: A highly anticipated rookie who stepped into a significant role in Cleveland's offense in 2025. Finished as RB24 heading into 2026 with legitimate upside if the Browns' offense develops around him and Concepcion. Some injury concern coming out of his rookie year. Contracted at $6 in year 2 of 5.
14835: One of the most physically gifted receivers in the NFL — 6'2", elite athleticism, YAC monster. Finished as WR17 in 2025 despite missing time with a concussion in the back half of the season. With Burrow healthy and the Bengals' offense clicking, Higgins has legitimate WR1 upside in any given week. Contracted at $23 in year 2 of 3.
14109: Washington's WR1 and one of the most consistent veterans in the game — finished as WR22 heading into 2026 after another reliable season in DC with Jayden Daniels at QB. McLaurin is a model of consistency, rarely boom-or-bust. Contracted at $26 in year 2 of 3, modestly above fair market for a WR22.
11675: Posted 60 catches, 789 yards, and 14 TDs for the Rams in 2025 — leading the NFL in receiving touchdowns. Now in the final year of his 2-year Rams deal at 33 years old. Route-running intelligence remains elite even late in his career. The TD production was remarkable; the volume (111 targets, 60 catches) was not what it once was. A contract year with real questions about his next stop.
16222: Emerged as a genuine TE1 option for Green Bay before a mid-season injury cut his 2025 short — at the time of injury he led the Packers in every receiving category (32-489-6 in 8 games). Healthy heading into 2026 and expected to reclaim his role as the focal point of Green Bay's passing game. TE5 ranking feels conservative if he stays on the field. Contracted at $14 in year 2 of 3.
17103: Second-year breakout candidate in Cleveland. Quietly emerged as one of the more intriguing young TEs in football in his rookie season — if Todd Monken can build an offense around him and Concepcion, Fannin could be a TE1 in 2026. Listed as TE6 heading into year 2. Contracted at $6 in year 2 of 5, significant long-term value if the production arrives.
15329: Five seasons in the league and finally living up to his draft pedigree in 2025 — 88 catches, 928 yards, 5 TDs on 118 targets, earning his first All-Pro selection. Drafted 4th overall in 2021, Pitts had been a consistent disappointment before this breakout. The Falcons placed the franchise tag on him heading into 2026. QB stability in Atlanta remains the perennial concern, but the production finally arrived.
16214: Back healthy after injuries limited him in 2025. LaPorta was one of the most exciting rookie TEs in recent memory in 2023, and the upside is still there in Detroit's pass-heavy scheme. TE8 heading into 2026 — a buy-low situation if the Lions stabilize their passing game. Contracted at $22 in year 4 of 5, significantly above fair market at his current ranking.
15799: Low-end TE1 in Dallas's high-scoring offense alongside Lamb and Pickens. Ferguson benefits from one of the better QB-receiver environments in the league and finished with consistent production in 2025. TE9 heading into 2026 — more of a role player than a star, but reliable weekly floor. Contracted at $12 in year 4 of 5.
16213: Has been maddeningly inconsistent throughout his career in Buffalo — the talent and situation have always been there, but injuries (12 and 13 games played in the last two seasons) keep him from fully capitalizing. TE10 heading into 2026. If healthy for 17 games, he's a top-6 TE. The injury risk is real. Contracted at $11 in year 4 of 5.
11244: Father Time remains undefeated, but Kelce is still finding ways to contribute at TE11 heading into 2026 — one of the great ironies of the dynasty era. Still benefits from Patrick Mahomes' ability to find him in critical moments. The question is whether he's a full-time starter anymore or a red-zone specialist. Contracted at $14 in year 2 of 3.
17099: Emerging young TE in the Chargers' offense who posted 49 catches, 664 yards, and 3 TDs in 2025. TE11 heading into 2026 with upside as Mike McDaniels takes over as OC. The new scheme could open up more opportunities for a receiving tight end. Contracted at $3 in year 3 of 5 — significant value at that price if his role expands.
17506: Dolphins WR drafted 94th overall as a developmental outside receiver. At 6'1" with good straight-line speed, Bell lands in Miami behind Tyreek Hill and a crowded depth chart. The target share is limited in year 1, but he's in a pass-heavy offense that will need weapons as the roster turns over. Bench depth now with starter upside in year 2-3.
17503: Steelers WR at pick 47 who steps into a Pittsburgh passing game that lost Diontae Johnson and needs receiver development. At 6'2" with strong contested-catch ability, Bernard profiles as a boundary receiver and red-zone threat. DK Metcalf commands outside attention — Bernard could benefit from volume on the opposite side. Viable bench stash with real WR3 upside in year 2.
17482: RB7 in the rookie class, drafted 122nd by Las Vegas. Steps into a backfield where Josh Jacobs departed for Green Bay, making Washington one of the more intriguing late-round additions. His receiving ability is a genuine asset in an already receiver-friendly Raiders offense. Bench depth with legitimate starter upside if he wins the job in camp.
17476: RB4 in the rookie class, drafted by Tennessee. Lands behind Tony Pollard on the depth chart but at 216 lbs with elite vision and pass-catching chops, Singleton profiles as a feature back within two seasons. The Titans are building around Cam Ward — Singleton fits that long-term timeline. Bench depth in 2026 with legitimate RB1 upside by 2027.
17514: 49ers WR at pick 33 who steps into San Francisco's receiver-friendly system alongside Ricky Pearsall. At 6'1" with strong athleticism and route fluency, Stribling fits Kyle Shanahan's motion-heavy scheme that consistently generates open looks. Year 1 ceiling is limited behind Pearsall and Aiyuk, but the situation is excellent for development. Bench depth with a high upside trajectory.
17481: RB8 in the rookie class, drafted by Minnesota at pick 198. Lands behind Aaron Jones, who is in the final year of his deal — opening a clear succession path in Minnesota's physical offensive identity. Compact, powerful runner who won't rush the starting role in 2026 but could be the Vikings' RB1 as early as 2027. Low-cost bench stash with excellent long-term value.
17567: TE3 in the rookie class, drafted by New Orleans. Delp arrives as a reliable in-line TE who showed receiving chops at Georgia — 38 catches, 480 yards in 2025. Juwan Johnson is ahead of him on the depth chart, but the Saints' offense has historically used multiple TEs. Step one is establishing himself on the roster; the path to starting production opens within two years. Bench depth with real upside.
17478: RB6 in the rookie class, drafted 187th by Washington. Lands alongside J.K. Dobbins and Brian Robinson in a crowded backfield, which limits his immediate ceiling. However, his receiving ability — 47 catches at Penn State in 2025 — makes him a candidate for a split role even in year 1 as a passing-down back. Bench depth with legitimate long-term starter potential.
17509: WR10 in the rookie class, drafted by Carolina at pick 83. Brazzell is a lean, athletic receiver who posted 63-802-7 at Army in 2025 — impressive production from a non-power program.
